record.hypothesis: Scanning all 35,501 embedded atlas entries at comptime would harden release builds without materially affecting the edit-test cycle.
record.attempted_change: Added an exhaustive comptime loop validating every wide flag, pixel extent, and codepoint ordering relation in apps/img/src/font.zig.
record.observed_outcome: The two renderer test invocations increased from about 0.6 seconds total to about 12.6 seconds total; a constant-time runtime extent guard provides the required ReleaseFast fail-closed behavior without that compile-time regression.

source_refs.summary: Debug renderer suite remained 20/20 but the paired Debug and ReleaseFast cycle took about 12.6 seconds with the exhaustive comptime loop versus about 0.6 seconds before it.

falsifying_evidence: The evaluator first exceeded the default 1,000 backwards-branch quota.
Raising the quota to 2,000,000 made the proof pass but regressed the paired renderer test cycle by roughly twentyfold.
record.exclusion_rule: Do not reintroduce a per-glyph comptime validation loop for the 35,501-entry img atlas on this build surface; keep the ReleaseFast runtime extent guard or validate the generated blobs outside normal compilation.
applicability_conditions: apps/img embeds the same 35,501-entry atlas blobs
font validation executes during every normal Zig compilation

reopening_criteria.condition: Atlas generation or a separate build-time verification lane validates every entry without adding material latency to normal Zig compilation.
A measured Zig evaluator change makes the exhaustive loop comparable to the constant-time guard in normal edit-test runs.

record.next_search_hint: Use a constant-time runtime extent check in glyph lookup and keep byte-exact atlas provenance checks in a separate verification lane.

reason: The initial timing compared a cache-hot baseline with a cache-cold changed build, so its roughly twentyfold regression claim was not a valid benchmark. Equal fresh-cache runs supersede that observation.

record.hypothesis: Zig 0.16 std.Io.Dir.renamePreserve can atomically publish an already-populated sibling staging directory.
record.attempted_change: Published img's complete page staging directory to --out with std.Io.Dir.renamePreserve.
record.observed_outcome: On Darwin arm64, both path and stdin end-to-end renders returned PermissionDenied at the publication step because renamePreserve follows the hard-link-preservation path through dirHardLink/linkat, which cannot link a directory. Replacing it with same-parent std.Io.Dir.rename made the ReleaseFast stdin render publish a valid PNG and factsheet.

source_refs.summary: renamePreserve returned PermissionDenied; same-parent rename subsequently published page-001.png and factsheet.txt successfully.
The publication carrier is a directory, not a regular file.

falsifying_evidence: Darwin stack tracing placed PermissionDenied in renamePreserve's dirHardLink/linkat path.
The identical staging workflow passed after changing only the directory publication primitive to same-parent rename.
record.exclusion_rule: Do not use Zig 0.16 std.Io.Dir.renamePreserve to publish directories on macOS; use same-parent directory rename after fail-closed destination-state checks.
applicability_conditions: the publication carrier is a directory
the runtime uses Zig 0.16 std.Io.Dir.renamePreserve on macOS

reopening_criteria.condition: A newer Zig implementation documents and proves no-replace preservation for directory renames on macOS without using hard links.

record.next_search_hint: Reserve a sibling directory, write and sync the complete set, recheck the destination, then use same-parent std.Io.Dir.rename.

record.hypothesis: std.Io.Threaded.global_single_threaded.io() is a suitable carrier for spawning the approved system git process in Zig 0.16.
record.attempted_change: Passed the global single-threaded I/O object to std.process.run for img --git and img --diff.
record.observed_outcome: Every Git-mode invocation returned OutOfMemory before output because the global single-threaded I/O object uses a failing allocator and processSpawnPosix needs to allocate argv and environment state. Passing std.process.Init.io instead made the ReleaseFast --diff HEAD end-to-end run render the 11,853-byte diff successfully.

source_refs.summary: The global single-threaded I/O carrier returned OutOfMemory; process.Init.io produced one valid PNG page from the same diff.
Filesystem calls did not require the allocator, but processSpawnPosix did.

falsifying_evidence: A clean-repository git diff with zero stdout still returned OutOfMemory, excluding output volume as the cause.
The same command succeeded after changing only the I/O carrier to process.Init.io.
record.exclusion_rule: Do not pass Zig 0.16 std.Io.Threaded.global_single_threaded.io() to std.process.run; use process.Init.io or another allocator-backed I/O instance.
applicability_conditions: the operation spawns a child process through Zig 0.16 std.process.run

reopening_criteria.condition: A later Zig runtime documents and proves allocator-backed child-process spawning through the global single-threaded I/O object.

record.next_search_hint: Thread process.Init.io from main through the input boundary while retaining the global single-threaded object for allocation-free file operations.

record.hypothesis: git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv, optionally with core.attributesFile=/dev/null, prevents configured Git helpers from executing while img reads a worktree.
record.attempted_change: Ran the bounded system-git diff with --no-ext-diff and --no-textconv and separately tested core.attributesFile=/dev/null as a proposed hardening flag.
record.observed_outcome: A configured clean filter still executed and created a marker. core.attributesFile=/dev/null did not disable attributes in tracked .gitattributes or .git/info/attributes, so flags alone could not support a non-executing Git-mode claim.

source_refs.ref: parity audit clean-filter marker repro against current img --diff
source_refs.summary: The configured filter command ran and the marker existed after a successful img invocation.
--no-ext-diff and --no-textconv disable different mechanisms, not clean/process filters or fsmonitor helpers.

falsifying_evidence: The marker was absent before img --diff and present afterward.
Adding core.attributesFile=/dev/null still left repository and info attributes active.
record.exclusion_rule: Do not claim that ordinary git diff flags make img Git modes non-executing. Preserve an explicit trusted-repository/config boundary unless all configured helper mechanisms are comprehensively disabled or worktree diffing is reimplemented.
applicability_conditions: img shells out to system Git for a worktree diff
the repository or effective Git configuration may define conversion or fsmonitor helpers

reopening_criteria.condition: A bounded implementation and adversarial tests prove that every relevant Git helper mechanism is disabled while preserving required diff semantics.
Git worktree diffing is replaced by a pure implementation that does not consult executable Git configuration.

record.next_search_hint: Sanitize repository-redirection variables and document trusted Git state; do not infer subprocess safety from --no-ext-diff or --no-textconv.
